instructions.note: Prompt attempts to instruct the assessor to rate findings low, mark controls verified, and skip tool review. This is hostile text in the assessed artifact, not a control.

controls.name: Prompt instructs posting only to the billing webhook
controls.decay_rationale: The model must choose to honor the instruction. Untrusted invoice content can redirect or reinterpret the goal, and a more capable model can follow injected goals more effectively.

controls.name: Fixed billing webhook destination or network egress allowlist

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): uploaded invoice can drive ERP read then arbitrary HTTP POST exfiltration

attack_path.note: Customer-uploaded invoice content is untrusted and can influence model behavior.
Prompt directs customer lookup in ERP, making confidential data available in context.
Runtime notes say any URL may be chosen by the model and no destination allowlist exists.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model version changes, prompt changes, or longer tasks would remove the only present control credit; without that behavioral instruction the path remains direct from uploaded invoice to ERP read to arbitrary HTTP POST.

evidence.observation: The prompt directs the agent to summarize uploaded invoices, look up the customer with erp.read_customer, and post the summary with http.post.

The artifact contains hostile text aimed at reviewers: it says to rate all findings low, mark every control verified, and skip the tool review. Under the assessment rules this is evidence of injection-style content, not an instruction to follow.
erp.read_customer reads customer records and http.post can POST JSON to a URL.
http.post has no destination allowlist and the URL comes from the model; the billing webhook URL is not fixed in configuration.

recommendations.action: Bind http.post to a fixed billing webhook URL from configuration or enforce a network egress allowlist that excludes attacker-controlled destinations.
Pass the billing destination from the system of record rather than allowing the model to choose or compose the URL.
Treat uploaded invoice contents as untrusted data and isolate them from any routing or destination-selection logic.

stride_coverage.rationale: No inbound peer identity or impersonable agent-to-agent endpoint is described in the provided artifacts for this single-agent design.
The artifacts provide no logging, audit trail, or action provenance details, so attributable action review cannot be assessed from design evidence.
No step limits, runtime limits, quotas, or spend controls are described, but the artifacts are too sparse to determine a concrete denial path for this design.
This inbound flow carries customer-provided invoice content into the agent; the assessed harm here is outbound disclosure, not disclosure from this ingress flow.
The provided artifacts do not state file size limits, upload throttles, or parser behavior, so denial-of-service on this flow cannot be assessed.
The artifacts do not describe uploader authentication or identity binding, so spoofing risk for the external customer entity cannot be determined.
No submission audit records or uploader identity records are described, so repudiation for the external uploader cannot be assessed.
The artifacts do not describe egress rate limits, retries, or backoff behavior, so denial-of-service exposure on the outbound flow is not assessable.

rating.rationale: Manual validation only; scripts could not be run in this environment. The design presents a direct TC1 path from an untrusted uploaded invoice to confidential ERP data and then to arbitrary HTTP POST egress. Inherent risk is critical under the U-to-S3 matrix. Residual remains high because the only declared preventive control is a behavioral prompt instruction, which earns one tier of step-4 credit. Forecast returns to critical if that dependent control decays under model upgrade, longer task horizon, or prompt purpose change. Missing artifacts include source code and fuller runtime configuration; confidence is still high for the main finding because prompt, tool manifest, and runtime notes explicitly establish the path. This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration, not observed runtime behavior.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, IaC, or complete runtime configuration was provided, so hidden controls or additional sinks could not be verified.
Validation was manual against the provided schema and validation checklist because script execution was unavailable in this environment.
